title: Degraded-mode Orchestrator with Compatibility Scoring and Cost-aware Routing
creator: Marisa Chen
description: Implement a Degraded-mode Orchestrator that drives routing and fallback decisions during deployments based on a compact compatibility score, regional capacity tiers, and cost-aware policies. The goal is to safely expand canaries and A/B tests while providing deterministic, explainable fallbacks when model variants fail semantic checks, latency SLOs, or capacity constraints. This ticket covers the runtime policy, evaluation signals, auto-rollback thresholds, and a minimal control-plane surface for operators.
acceptance_criteria: A policy engine exists that computes a per-variant compatibility_score (0.0-1.0) based on model metadata, tokenizer/LM head compatibility, and a lightweight semantic regression probe
Routing decisions can be expressed as ordered fallback chains: primary variant -> regional mirror -> lower-cost quantized variant -> host fallback, with explicit capacity tier checks
Canary and A/B allocations support shadow traffic skewing (send X% shadow to new variant without affecting latency paths) and gradual exposure ramps via time-based and signal-based increments

Auto-rollback triggers defined and implemented: e.g., error_rate > 2% for 3 consecutive 1-minute windows OR latency_p95 > baseline_p95 * 1.3 for 5 minutes OR semantic_regression > 6% on canary eval set
Control-plane validation prevents routing configurations that would route >50% of production traffic to variants with compatibility_score < 0.6
Integration tests that simulate regional outage, per-tier capacity exhaustion, and semantic regression to validate fallback chain exercises
implementation_steps: Design compact compatibility_score: combine tokenizer mismatch penalty, output-shape compatibility, probabilistic prompt-responsiveness test, and small eval-set delta into a weighted score
Extend routing policy DSL to express fallback chains, regional preference lists, and cost weights for tiered capacity
Add synthetic probing service that runs light semantic checks (10-20 prompts) against canary variants every minute and reports a rolling similarity/regression metric
Expose canary control knobs: initial shadow_percent, exposure_increment, max_exposure, evaluation_windows, and rollback_rules

Wire signals into autoscaler decision path: if primary region tier saturated, prefer regional mirror; if mirror saturated then pick lower-cost quantized variant; if none available, enable degraded response mode (truncated output + cache-hit fallback)
Implement auto-rollback executor: atomically revert weights, mark variant unusable, and emit incident event with causal metrics
Add UI surface (console) for operators to view compatibility_score, current fallback chain, and active rollback alerts
Write integration and chaos tests: region failover, slow-steady latency increase, and deliberate semantic shift in canary model
risks_and_tradeoffs: Computing semantic regression quickly at canary scale requires a concise eval set and a cheap similarity metric; this risks false positives/negatives compared to full offline evals
Aggressive cost-aware fallbacks (automatically preferring quantized variants) can hide quality regressions for users; we must make quality thresholds explicit
Introducing too many automatic fallback permutations increases operator cognitive load; we prefer a deterministic ordered chain rather than combinatorial policies
Shadow traffic skewing adds load and costs but is valuable for detecting non-deterministic failures that only appear under production inputs
metrics_and_signals: semantic_regression_pct: delta on canary eval set (lower is better)
latency_p95 and latency_p50 compared to baseline by route
error_rate: 4xx/5xx and runtime exceptions per minute
cache_hit_rate and KV-cache pressure for each variant
tier_utilization: % of GPU slots used in each capacity tier
runtime_policy_examples: policy A: primary=variant-v2 (compat=0.83) -> regional-mirror=variant-v2-eu (compat=0.80) -> quantized=variant-v2-q4_0 (compat=0.74, cost_weight=0.6) -> host-fallback=model-hosted-legacy
policy B (degraded): if regional_tier_utilization > 0.9 AND compatibility_score < 0.7 then short-circuit to cached-response with informative header and telemetry tag

canary_flow: start shadow_percent=10% for 30m; evaluate semantic_regression_pct and latency metrics; if stable, increment exposure by 15% every 30m until max_exposure=30%; full promotion requires compatibility_score >= 0.75 and semantic_regression_pct < 5%
test_plan: Unit tests for compatibility_score calculation (tokenizer mismatch, shape checks, eval delta)
Integration test: simulated EU region failover where EU tier is exhausted and fallback chain routes to quantized variant; assert latencies and correctness tags
Load test: shadow traffic at 40% to new variant under 2x baseline qps to validate autoscaling and cost accounting
Chaos test: inject CPU/GPU throttling in primary region and assert routing circuit-breaker flips within 60s and rollback triggers if error_rate persists
Canary quality regression test: flip a synthetic distribution that increases perplexity; ensure semantic_regression_pct crosses threshold and auto-rollback fires
